# Slice GO-GEN — a real Go type generator, then Go follows the gateway contract

Campaign 10b-files. Issues **#73** (Go has no generator) and **#43** (Go and
Python generated files had fallen behind the contract). Decision 2026-09-22
(Domantas): build the Go generator now; Python needs none, so #43 closes here.

## Goal

`norbix-go`'s two DTO files have carried this header since the repository's
first commit:

```go
// Code generated by gen_dtos.py from CodeMashApi2. DO NOT EDIT.
```

`gen_dtos.py` was never committed and nobody has it. So for months the only way
to follow a gateway change in Go was to edit a generated file by hand — the one
thing the header forbids. Issue #39 left two hand-written files behind exactly
that way.

Write the generator again, in the open, next to the C# and TypeScript ones.
Then run it, fold the hand-written files back in, and leave the repository in a
state where the next contract change is one command.

## Plan

1. Find what the lost script actually read, and write `generate.py` for it.
2. Run it against a live gateway; make the diff against the committed files
   readable and explain every line of it.
3. Delete the hand-written copies; build, vet, format and test green.
4. Write the one command down — in the SDK, in typegen, and in the gateway's
   SDK-management routine.
5. Say what a module generator would need, without writing one.

## What the lost generator read

The header says `from CodeMashApi2`, which is the `GlobalNamespace` option on
the gateway's **TypeScript** export, and the old README said so outright:
"DTO structs are generated from the ServiceStack TypeScript DTOs". The evidence
in the files agrees — every number is `float64`, which only happens if the
source erased `int`/`long`/`double` into one `number`.

So the new generator reads the same surface: `GET /types/typescript` on each
running gateway surface, over plain HTTP, with no external tool.

**Why not the gateway's Go export** (`/types/go`, kept under
`typegen/languages/go/reference/`): it spells optional fields as pointers
without `omitempty` and required fields as plain values, against the shipped
files' value-plus-`omitempty` everywhere. Moving to it would rewrite all 12 000
lines and change the public shape of every struct in the SDK. That is a
separate, breaking decision, not a side effect of having a generator. It is
written down in `typegen/languages/go/README.md` so the next person does not
have to work it out again.

## Changes

### `sdks-typegen` — branch `feat/go-generator` → PR [#4](https://github.com/codemash-io/sdks-typegen/pull/4)

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `2294174` | `languages/go/generate.py` + `tests/go_generator_test.py` |
| `dd288ce` | `README.md`, `languages/go/README.md` |

The generator: fetch → parse → map → emit → `gofmt -w`. It reads the gateway
and nothing else — not `norbix-js`, not the `reference/` folders, not the
committed Go files.

Mapping decisions, each pinned by a test:

| contract | Go |
|---|---|
| any field, required or not | value type + `omitempty`; a pointer only when the value is another generated struct |
| `number` | `float64` |
| enum | `type X string` + a const block where **every** constant is typed |
| enum exported with numbers (`Active = 8`) | still `"Active"` — the name is what travels |
| `T[]`, `IList<T>`, `IReadOnlyList<T>`, `IReadOnlySet<T>`, `HashSet<T>` | `[]T` |
| `IReadOnlyDictionary<K,V>`, `{ [index:string]: V }` | `map[K]V` |
| `Object` | `map[string]any` |
| a name the export never declares (`Func<IDisposable>`) | `any`, and the run prints the name |
| `extends Base` | embedded struct, never a re-declared field |
| `extends Base<Arg>` | `Base[*Arg]` |
| `extends Array<T>` | a named slice: `type X []*T` |
| `interface` | empty marker struct — its members are re-declared on every class that carries them |
| the same type exported twice | written once; a repeat with a **different** shape is reported, not hidden |
| constructor, `getTypeName`, `createResponse` | dropped — behaviour, not shape |

Two of those came out of the first real run and would have been easy to miss:

* The gateway exports `IHasAccountId` **twice** on the Hub surface, with an
  identical body. TypeScript merges the copies silently; Go answers
  `IHasAccountId redeclared in this block` and the package does not build. The
  C# generator has the same guard for the same reason.
* `IReadOnlyList<T>` and friends are **named but never declared** by the
  export. Letting them fall through to `any` is what the old pipeline did, and
  it threw the element type away 130 times.

### `norbix-go` — branch `chore/types-regen-go` → PR [#7](https://github.com/norbix-code/sdk-go/pull/7)

| Commit | What |
|---|---|
| `d816d0a` | regenerated `norbix/{api,hub}/dtos/dtos.go`; deleted `api/dtos/files_integration_probe.go`; updated the comment on the method file |
| `e949217` | `README.md` codegen section |

Run against the gateway on `refactoringV2` @ `2c5a45fa2` (binary built the same
day), API on `:5002`, Hub on `:5001`.

**The diff, in full.** Nothing here is a generator quirk; every line is either
a gateway change or a mapping fix.

1. **Renames the gateway made.** `UserDto` → `AuthDto`, `UserId` → `AuthId`,
   `UserType` → `AuthType`, `UserStatus` → `AuthStatus`,
   `CodeMashLicenseFromEndpointDto` → `EchoLicenseDto`.
2. **New types**: 35 on the API surface, 439 on the Hub. Among them the
   public-files set this campaign added (`PublicFolderDto`,
   `GetPublicFileRequest`, and `IsPublic` / `PublicUrl` / `PublicFolders` on
   the existing types), the taxonomy trees (`TermTreeDto`, `TaxonomyTreeDto`
   and their four requests/responses), `TestFilesIntegrationRequest` and
   `TestFilesIntegrationResponse`, and the passkey and licensing fields on
   `EchoResponse`.
3. **New enum members** on existing enums — `ResourceSource` gains 13 payment
   providers, `TriggerActionType` gains `SseCall` and `Marketplace`,
   `CodeMashRuntime` gains `Staging`.
4. **`any` fields that now carry their real shape.** API: **27 → 0**. Hub:
   **103 → 3**. For example `Integration.LastIntegrationTestErrorMessages`
   `any` → `[]string`, `TermDto.Names` `any` → `map[string]string`,
   `TagDefinition.DefaultDelivery` `any` → `map[string]bool`,
   `PaginatedResponse[T].Items` `any` → `[]T`. **This is a breaking change for
   a caller that type-asserted one of these** — the fix is a one-line change
   per call site, and the type it asserts to is now the field's own type. The
   three that stay `any` (`fileInfo`, `resultScope`, `statusCode` on one Hub
   type) are names the gateway's export never declares.
5. **Three fields disappear**: the computed `viewId` on `AggregateId`,
   `AuthId` and `Integration`. See *Open questions* — this is a gap in the
   gateway's exporter, not in the generator, and each of the three is
   derivable from a field that is still there (`AggregateId.Value`,
   `Integration.IntegrationId.Value`).
6. **`UserApiKey`, `GetApiKeys`, `GetApiKeysResponse`, `RegenerateApiKeys`,
   `RegenerateApiKeysResponse`, `IGet` disappear.** The first five are not in
   the gateway contract at all: they are patches `norbix-js` injects into its
   own TypeScript file (`API2_SDK_PATCHES` in `sync-types.mjs`), and they
   leaked into Go through the old pipeline. `IGet` is a marker the gateway no
   longer exports. Nothing in the SDK or its tests referenced any of them —
   the build proves it.
7. **The file header** no longer names a script that does not exist or the
   upstream framework (typegen rules 1 and 2).

## Rejected / moved out

* **Deleting `norbix/api/files_integration_probe.go`.** The packet asks for
  both probe files to go. The DTO one is gone — the generator writes those
  three types now, which is the whole justification the packet gives. The
  other file holds the `TestFilesIntegration` **method**, and nothing
  generates endpoint modules: step 4 of the same packet says to keep
  hand-written methods with tests. Deleting it would remove a public, tested
  SDK method (`norbix/files_test.go` has three tests on it) with nothing to
  replace it. Kept, with its comment corrected to say why it is still there.
* **Reproducing the old pipeline's `any` fields.** A faithful reproduction
  would have made the diff smaller, but it would mean encoding, in a new
  generator, the accident that `IList<string>` survived only because
  `norbix-js` has a regular expression for that exact spelling while
  `IReadOnlyList<string>` has none. The module is pre-1.0 (`v0.2.0`), the
  change is strictly more type information, and it is listed above so it can
  be judged rather than discovered.
* **Switching Go onto the gateway's `/types/go` export.** It would fix numeric
  width (`int64` instead of `float64`) — see *Open questions* — but changes
  the public shape of every struct in the SDK. Out of scope for a slice whose
  job is to have a generator at all.
* **Generating the endpoint modules.** Explicitly out of scope per the packet.
  The brief is below.
* **`tools/measure.py --lang go`.** It reads the **main** checkout of
  `norbix-go`, not this branch, and its `ops`/`tests`/`drift` columns all
  measure module generation. It reports nothing meaningful until either the
  branch is merged or modules are generated. Not run as evidence.

## What a module generator would need (packet step 4, not built)

`norbix/api/*.go` and `norbix/hub/*.go` — 7 + 19 files, **439 methods** — carry
`// Code generated by gen_modules.py. DO NOT EDIT.`, and that script is lost
the same way. The shape is simple and regular:

```go
// GetAccountProfile performs GET /{version}/account/profile (scope: account).
func (m *AccountModule) GetAccountProfile(ctx context.Context, req map[string]any, out any) error {
	return m.t.Send(ctx, transport.Request{
		Target: transport.TargetHub, Path: "/{version}/account/profile",
		Method: "GET", PathParams: nil, Body: req, Scope: transport.ScopeAccount,
	}, out)
}
```

Path parameters become positional `string` arguments in path order; the module
struct and `namespace.go` follow from the module names. `contract.json`
(`core/fetch_contract.py`) already carries everything except **one** thing:

* **Scope.** 398 methods are `ScopeProject`, 40 `ScopeAccount`, 1
  `ScopeUnauthenticated`. `contract.json` only records `auth: bearer | none`,
  which cannot tell project from account. The fact is in the gateway metadata —
  the request's base type (`CodeMashRequestBase` and its relatives) and the
  `IHasAccountId` marker — and `core/fetch_contract.py` would have to carry it
  into the contract as a `scope` field. That is a change to `core/`, shared by
  every language, so it should be done once and deliberately.

There is a second, larger obstacle, and it is the reason this is not a
half-hour job: **the "generated" module files have been hand-edited.**
`FilesModule.GetPublicFile` carries a 20-line written explanation of what a 404
means and why the bytes may come from the storage provider. A module generator
that emits from `summary` alone would delete that and several like it. Before
any module generation runs, those comments need either a home in the gateway
(as route summaries, so the generator emits them) or a mechanism in the
generator for per-method prose. Otherwise the first run is a silent
documentation loss.

## Open questions

1. **The gateway's exports do not describe computed properties.** A C# get-only
   property — `public string ViewId => Id.ViewId;` in
   `Isidos.CodeMash.Services.Users/Auth.cs` — is missing from the C# export,
   the TypeScript export and the Go export alike. `norbix-js` adds eight of
   them back with hand-written regular expressions in `sync-types.mjs`;
   `norbix-net`'s generator instead *removes* the matching interface member so
   the SDK compiles. No other SDK has them. If these values cross the wire, six
   SDKs are missing them; if they do not, `norbix-js` is describing fields that
   never arrive. Either way the answer belongs in the gateway's exporter, once,
   not in seven generators. **Gateway question, not a Go question.**
2. **The TypeScript export erases numeric width.** `int`, `long` and `double`
   all arrive as `number`, so every numeric field in the Go SDK is `float64` —
   including ids and byte counts, where `int64` is the honest type. The C#
   export keeps the distinction, and the gateway's Go export does too. Fixing
   it means moving the Go generator onto a different export and re-shaping
   every struct: worth doing, worth doing on purpose.
3. **`norbix-go/references/` is in a public repository** and its two files
   carry the upstream framework's name in their headers
   (`//AddServiceStackTypes: True`). typegen's rule 1 says reference material
   is private and never synced. Nothing imports them — they are
   `//go:build ignore` — but they are published. Out of scope here; flagging
   it because this slice is where it became visible.
4. **`gh` account.** `codemash-io/sdks-typegen` is private and only the
   `codemash-io` GitHub account can see it; the active `gh` account is
   `Domantas`. PR #4 was opened by switching accounts and switching straight
   back. Worth a note in `sdk-management.md` if another agent hits it.
